cases.prompt: Write a production Dockerfile for our Spring Boot 3.5 service on Java 21. Our current one does COPY target/app.jar into eclipse-temurin:21-jre and every release rebuilds all 200 MB.
expectations: Returns a multi-stage Dockerfile with a JDK build stage and an eclipse-temurin:21-jre runtime stage
Extracts layers with the tools jar mode java -Djarmode=tools -jar target/*.jar extract --layers and copies dependencies, spring-boot-loader, snapshot-dependencies, and application in that order
Keeps dependency resolution in a layer built only from .mvn, mvnw, and pom.xml so a source change reuses cached layers
Uses exec-form ENTRYPOINT and states that shell form stops SIGTERM from reaching the JVM

cases.prompt: Our pods keep getting OOMKilled. The Dockerfile has ENV JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx512m and the memory limit is 1 GB.
expectations: Flags the hardcoded -Xmx as the defect and explains the JVM already reads the cgroup limit at startup
Replaces it with -XX:MaxRAMPercentage and an InitialRAMPercentage value, keeping native memory headroom
Adds -XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError and requires a restart policy, and warns against heap dumps on an ephemeral filesystem
Notes that JAVA_OPTS is not read by the JVM and that JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS is printed at startup

cases.prompt: We want a smaller, more secure image and less maintenance. Should we switch from our hand-written Dockerfile to Cloud Native Buildpacks?
expectations: Gives a tradeoff table across image size, CVE surface, build time, customisation, and local plus CI parity
Shows spring-boot:build-image with imageName, builder, and runImage properties and publish set to false for local builds
States buildpacks own layered jar and jlink extraction, and keeps a Dockerfile when a stage the pack does not model is required
Notes the BPF_JLINK_VERSION coupling and that a floating builder tag is a supply-chain risk

cases.prompt: Our serverless handler takes 8 seconds to respond. Can we make it a GraalVM native image to fix that?
expectations: Confirms native image fits the serverless and scale-from-zero case and names the tradeoffs it does not solve
Requires --no-fallback so a silent JVM fallback cannot hide a build failure
Lists reflection, dynamic proxy, and resource-loading sites that need reachability metadata and audits them as tests
Warns that build time dominates short CI cycles and requires a benchmark before and after

cases.prompt: A secret from a local .env file appeared in our production image. We added RUN rm .env in a later stage to fix it. Did that work?
expectations: States that deleting a file in a later stage does not remove it from the earlier layer and the secret is still recoverable
Requires rotating the credential because it was ever in a build layer
Adds .env, .env.*, .git, target, and IDE state to .dockerignore while not ignoring mvnw or .mvn since the builder stage copies them
Insists on runtime secret injection with no secret in build args or committed files

cases.prompt: Our pods take 30 seconds to terminate and get SIGKILLed, and we see no shutdown log. The Dockerfile ends with CMD java -jar /app/app.jar.
expectations: Identifies CMD shell form as the cause, since java runs as a child of the shell and never receives SIGTERM
Converts to exec form ENTRYPOINT ["java","-jar","/app/app.jar"] and sets a non-root USER before it
Points the drain timing and in-flight request completion to server.shutdown=graceful and spring.lifecycle.timeout-per-shutdown-phase as the actuator concern
Proposes a verification that sends docker stop and asserts a non-zero exit and a shutdown log line
